title: Admin Handoff Bridge + Playflow Suggester (ML-assisted runbook stitching)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: On-call handoffs frequently lose context and require a human to stitch together multiple runbook fragments. This costs time during incidents and introduces variance in remediation quality.

Goal: Build an "Admin Handoff Bridge" service that converts tickets/alerts into a draft executable playflow (runbook-as-task) and surfaces ML-suggested remediation steps ranked by telemetry-derived confidence. The bridge should produce a safe, auditable, permission-scoped playflow that a responder can review, dry-run, or execute.

Scope: MVP covers (1) ticket -> playflow conversion for common incident classes (cpu, model OOM, degraded latency, stuck worker), (2) an ML-based suggester that ranks candidate steps and provides confidence/why-explanation, (3) dry-run simulation with guardrails, (4) RBAC-checked execution and audit logging, (5) Console integration to preview and accept suggestions.

Out of scope for MVP: automated escalation across org boundaries, full natural-language generation for arbitrary runbooks, and persistent learner pipelines (we will log feedback for future model fine-tuning).
acceptance_criteria: Ticket -> playflow conversion produces a well-formed JSON playflow with typed steps and input validation
Suggester returns at least 3 candidate remediation steps with confidence scores and short rationale
Dry-run mode simulates side effects and returns a summarized impact report without mutating prod systems
Execution path enforces RBAC and records an immutable audit entry with requestor, step results, and artifacts
Console displays suggested playflow, allows step reordering, and supports one-click dry-run and one-click execute (subject to permissions)
End-to-end latency for conversion+suggestion stays under 2s median for mocked tickets (MVP target)
updates: 2025-02-10: RFC posted. Collected sample tickets from SRE and Support (20 incidents) and annotated expected playflows.
2025-02-14: Design sync with PM/Design. Decided on playflow JSON schema (typed steps, optional preconditions, compensating actions, safe-timeouts). Confluence spec linked.
2025-02-18: Prototype API stub implemented (handoff-service POST /v1/handoff/convert) that returns a minimal playflow for CPU incidents.
2025-02-22: ML prototype (handbook-suggester-v0) integrated locally. Uses telemetry features: runbook-usage, past-fix-success, latency delta patterns to rank steps.

2025-02-25: UX mockups delivered. Console panel to accept/reject suggestions; will show confidence band and example traces. Design feedback: surface risky steps in red and require explicit confirmation.

2025-02-28: End-to-end prototype demo with SRE. Two main concerns: (1) permission scoping for playflow steps that require privileged tokens, (2) ensuring idempotency of automated steps. Added token-scope check in flow.
2025-03-01: PR opened for handoff-service core logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-auto/pull/142

2025-03-03: Blocked on SSO role mapping for service principal impersonation. Security team requested design for ephemeral credentials and HSM-backed signing for audit. Added to blockers and assigned security reviewer.
2025-03-03: Next: implement dry-run simulator, instrument telemetry metrics, and add a consent modal in Console for risky steps.
implementation_notes: Service: handoff-service (new lightweight Go service behind internal API gateway)
Endpoint: POST /v1/handoff/convert accepts ticket id + contextual artifacts (logs, traces, trace_ids) and returns playflow JSON and suggestions array
Suggester: handbook-suggester-v1 (offline-scoring model packaged as a microservice). For MVP we'll use a rules+light-ML hybrid to avoid hallucinations.
Playflow schema: steps[] with {id, type, command, inputs, preconditions, compensating_action, estimated_risk, default_timeout_ms}
Dry-run: simulator will call mock adapters for side-effectful steps and return simulated results. Simulator must be deterministic and isolated to internal sandbox namespaces.
RBAC: integrate with existing authz service. Each step should carry 'required_roles' and be validated at accept/execute time. Add service principal impersonation design for approved automated runs.
Telemetry: emit metrics handoff.suggestions.count, handoff.suggestions.confidence.hist, handoff.exec.duration, handoff.dryrun.impact_score
Logging: every generated playflow must be written to immutable ops-audit store with a pointer to associated ticket and artifacts (retain per compliance policy)
Safety: add an allowlist for automated-only steps (non-destructive ops) and require explicit confirmation for privileged/irreversible commands
test_plan: Unit tests for converters using the 20 annotated incidents dataset
Integration tests for suggestions with mocked telemetry features and deterministic ranking
End-to-end QA flow: create synthetic ticket -> convert -> dry-run -> accept -> simulated execute; validate audit log entries
Security review: threat model for ephemeral credential flow and audit signing
Canary rollout: enable feature flag for 'team-sre' org only and monitor handoff.suggestions.accept_rate and handoff.exec.failures for 72h
